stories.headline: Google's A2A Protocol Joins Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, Unifying Agent Standards With Anthropic's MCP
stories.summary: On August 20, 2026, Google's Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol formally joined the Linux Foundation-directed Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), placing it under the same neutral governance umbrella as Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP). The AAIF now counts over 250 members including AWS, Microsoft, Google, OpenAI, Bloomberg, and Cloudflare, consolidating the two dominant agent communication standards into one governed stack. For D&B, this is a direct validation of the 'be everywhere' neutrality strategy — a unified protocol stack lowers integration friction and makes D&B's MCP server and data layer more valuable as a plug-in across all compliant agent architectures, regardless of which platform wins.

stories.headline: IDC: 80% of B2B Tech Buyers Are Now Using AI Agents in Their Purchasing Process
stories.summary: New IDC research published in August 2026 confirms that eight in ten B2B technology buyers are already using AI agents as part of their purchasing process — not a forecast, but a current reality for procurement teams evaluating enterprise software and services right now. A separate IDC finding from the same period shows 45% of enterprise AI projects are still failing to deliver results, with CIOs demanding clearer ROI and defined governance for agentic deployments. This double signal — buyers automating discovery while most AI projects underdeliver — puts structured, trusted data like D&B's at the centre of the solution: agents that act on unreliable data will be fired, and those grounded in verified entity intelligence will win.

stories.headline: AWS Pushes Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Web Search to General Availability
stories.summary: On August 21, 2026, AWS moved Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to general availability, offering a managed server-side tool that lets enterprise AI agents fetch live, cited web knowledge without data leaving the customer's AWS cloud environment. The launch, initially available in US East (N. Virginia), is a clear signal that the major cloud providers are racing to make agentic retrieval production-ready and secure by default. For D&B, this is an accelerant: as Amazon Bedrock becomes a serious enterprise agent runtime, embedding D&B's data layer — including DUNS entity resolution and commercial graph — into Bedrock-native agent workflows becomes a high-value distribution vector in the 'be everywhere' model.

stories.headline: D&B Launches Agentic AI Capabilities for Compliance and Third-Party Risk, Cutting Processing Times by Up to 90%
stories.summary: Dun & Bradstreet announced in June 2026 new agentic capabilities embedded within its Risk Analytics platform and accessible via its MCP server, enabling organisations to automate onboarding, screening, and due diligence workflows — with processing times reduced by 70–90%. The offering combines verified D&B business identity data and models with AI agents, and is positioned for enterprises at all levels of AI maturity. This is D&B executing directly on its 'AI Decision Intelligence' strategy: entity resolution and verified commercial data as the trusted foundation that makes compliance agents both faster and defensible — not just automated, but explainable.

stories.headline: S&P Global Flags Slowing Commercial Credit Growth Globally as Geopolitical Stress Bites Central Europe and China
stories.summary: S&P Global's August 2026 Banking Risk Monthly Outlook reports that credit growth has slowed substantially in China during Q2 2026, prompting expectations that the PBOC will lower reserve requirements before year-end, while risk aversion is restraining lending growth across Central European banking sectors — partly driven by geopolitical disruptions including strikes on Iran and shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. The report paints a picture of simultaneous credit tightening across two major commercial lending regions at once. For D&B, this is a live use case for temporal risk analytics: commercial credit conditions are shifting quarter-by-quarter, and the ability to surface real-time Paydex and financial stress signals at the account level is exactly the differentiation that enterprise risk teams need when macro conditions deteriorate at speed.

stories.headline: Thomson Reuters Launches Proprietary LLM 'Thomson' for $40M — Trained on Its Own Legal Data
stories.summary: Thomson Reuters launched Thomson, its first in-house large language model, on August 24, built on an open-source foundation and trained on decades of Westlaw and Practical Law content for roughly $40 million — a fraction of what frontier labs spend. The model initially powers tabular document analysis inside CoCounsel Legal, with CoCounsel remaining a multi-model product that also pulls in third-party frontier models for other tasks. This is the clearest proof yet that proprietary data estates — not just compute budgets — are the real competitive moat in AI: the same structural argument D&B makes for its 600M+ business records and Paydex/DUNS assets.

stories.headline: Nvidia Reports Q2 Earnings: AI Data Center ROI Now Under One Year, VC Funding Tops $400B in H1
stories.summary: Nvidia's fiscal Q2 results, reported this week, included the striking management disclosure that return on invested capital for AI data centers has compressed to under one year even for facilities costing tens of billions of dollars — a figure that rationalises the continued hyperscaler spending sprint. Nvidia also highlighted that global VC funding in AI exceeded $400 billion in the first half of 2026 alone, with roughly 70% directed at compute infrastructure. The earnings underline that AI infrastructure economics are strengthening, not stalling — which supports continued enterprise AI adoption and, by extension, demand for the trusted data layer that makes those agents produce reliable outputs.

stories.headline: Emerald AI Raises $150M Series A at $1B Valuation — AI Meets Energy Grid
stories.summary: Washington D.C.-based Emerald AI closed an oversubscribed $150 million Series A on August 25, reaching a $1.05 billion valuation, co-led by Energize Capital and DCVC with participation from Nvidia, Samsung Ventures, Siemens, GE Vernova, Aramco Ventures, and In-Q-Tel among others. The company operates at the intersection of AI infrastructure and energy grid management — a sector that has moved from niche to critical as power constraints become the binding limit on AI buildout. The breadth of industrial and defence-adjacent investors (In-Q-Tel, GE Vernova, Aramco) signals that AI-energy convergence is now a national-security-grade infrastructure bet, not just a climate play.

stories.headline: US States Move to Regulate AI in High-Stakes Decisions — Employment, Housing, Finance in Scope
stories.summary: A Center for Democracy & Technology analysis published August 20 confirms that the 2026 state legislative session has produced meaningful movement on regulating automated decision systems in consequential contexts — employment, housing, finance, and education — alongside frontier model risk and third-party auditing requirements. The trend is running in parallel with the Trump administration's federal Executive Order, which is actively trying to preempt the patchwork of state rules by threatening to withhold federal funds from states that legislate independently. For D&B, whose Paydex scores and business data feed credit, supplier risk, and employment decisions, this regulatory direction reinforces the case for explainability-first, auditable AI outputs — a core D&B differentiator — as enterprises scramble to demonstrate compliance.
stories.source: Center for Democracy & Technology / Gunderson Dettmer

stories.headline: Andy Burnham Visits Kyiv on Ukraine Independence Day, Pledges SCALP Missile Support
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham travelled to Kyiv to mark Ukrainian Independence Day, where he announced that defence firm MBDA will release details on UK-made components for the SCALP missile to help Ukraine assemble the weapons domestically. The visit signals continuity in UK support for Ukraine under Burnham's premiership, which began after Keir Starmer resigned in June 2026. It also represents a significant step in front-line military-industrial cooperation between London and Kyiv.

stories.headline: Trump Administration Pressures UN to Back Major Budget and Workforce Cuts
stories.summary: The Trump administration is working to ensure the United Nations' incoming leadership will support sweeping budget reductions and staff cuts across the global body. The move is the latest in a sustained US effort to reshape multilateral institutions in line with administration priorities. It comes amid ongoing US-Iran hostilities and a broader pattern of American withdrawal from international frameworks.

stories.headline: NASA's Roman Space Telescope Encapsulated and Ready for August 30 Launch
stories.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has been sealed inside its Falcon Heavy fairing and cleared for a targeted liftoff on 30 August, just three days away. The powerful observatory is designed to probe dark matter, dark energy, and cosmic expansion, and could also discover thousands of exoplanets. The Artemis II crew were separately awarded the Congressional Space Medal of Honor this week for becoming the first humans to travel beyond the Moon in over 50 years.

stories.headline: PGA Tour and DP World Tour Planning Nine-Event Global Series From 2028
stories.summary: The PGA Tour and DP World Tour are reportedly working on plans for a nine-event global series that could reshape the men's professional golf calendar as early as 2028. Potential venues have been identified across England, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, France, Spain, Italy, Australia, South Africa and the Far East. The events would remain under the DP World Tour banner rather than becoming co-sanctioned, marking a significant step in the two tours' deepening alliance. Closer to home, the Betfred British Masters hosted by Sir Nick Faldo tees off today at The Belfry.

stories.headline: Premier League Off to a Chaotic Start — Hull Stun Man United, Brentford Thrash Spurs
stories.summary: The 2026–27 Premier League season opened with a series of surprises in Matchweek 1. Newly promoted Hull City beat Manchester United 2–0, Brentford hammered Spurs 3–0, and Liverpool came from behind twice to draw 2–2 with Newcastle. The transfer window remains open until 1 September, with the clock ticking on late deadline-day business.

stories.headline: France Clinch 2026 Six Nations Title With Last-Gasp Ramos Penalty Over England
stories.summary: France secured their 20th Six Nations title — and a second in succession — with a dramatic 48–46 victory over England in the final match of the tournament back in March, courtesy of a last-kick penalty from top scorer Thomas Ramos. Louis Bielle-Biarrey was named Player of the Tournament after scoring nine tries, a Six Nations record. England's title defence ended in heartbreak, with Ireland taking the Triple Crown. Attention now turns to the new Premiership franchise era, which kicks off on 25 September.

stories.headline: Scientists Crack Diamond Rain Mystery — and It Could Triple Fusion Energy Output
stories.summary: Physicists at the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, publishing in Nature Physics, have resolved a 20-year scientific mystery about how diamonds form inside ice giant planets like Neptune. By mimicking the extreme pressure and temperature conditions believed to produce diamond rain in planetary interiors, the team found the same physics could help triple fusion energy output. The finding bridges planetary science and practical clean energy research in a striking and unexpected way.

stories.headline: Microsoft's AI Earnings Signal: Clarity of Strategy, Lower Costs, Tangible Applications
stories.summary: Ben Thompson's August 25 Stratechery update flags Microsoft's Q2 2026 earnings as notable precisely because they showed something rare in the current AI cycle: a clear strategic thesis, falling unit costs, and AI applications that enterprise customers can actually point to. This matters beyond Microsoft — it is the first major signal that the capex supercycle is beginning to convert into measurable enterprise value, not just spend. For D&B, this is a green light: enterprise buyers who can now show internal AI ROI will accelerate procurement of the data layers — entity resolution, firmographics, risk scores — that make those AI applications defensible and accurate. The clarity-of-strategy framing also validates D&B's own positioning: neutrality and explainability are increasingly what CFOs demand before signing off on AI-dependent workflows.

stories.headline: AI M&A Has Shifted From 'Buying Models' to 'Buying Control Points'
stories.summary: A widely-circulated Substack analysis argues that the dominant question in 2025–2026 M&A is no longer 'who has the best model?' but 'who controls the layer every model, agent, or AI application must pass through?' — with data-center dealmaking hitting records and acquirers chasing infrastructure choke points over raw capability. The piece documents a structural shift where strategic value is accruing to whoever sits between AI consumers and AI producers. This directly validates D&B's 'be everywhere' Visa analogy: the DUNS number and entity resolution graph are precisely the kind of control-point asset that every agentic workflow must pass through for trust and accuracy. It also signals that D&B's data assets carry genuine M&A premium characteristics — proprietary, non-replicable, and compounding.

stories.headline: AI M&A in H2 2026: Application-Layer Valuations Correcting, Proprietary Data Commands Premium
stories.summary: BCG's mid-2026 M&A analysis finds that global dealmaking is rebounding from strategic necessity as AI reshapes competitive dynamics, but warns that acquirers without a clear thesis risk overpaying for narratives. The report identifies H2 2026 as the moment when application-layer AI valuations correct and a wider range of targets become available — raising both the reward for disciplined buyers and the penalty for undisciplined ones. For D&B, this is a dual signal: as pure AI-wrapper companies struggle to attract serious M&A interest, firms with proprietary data moats (exactly D&B's profile) are seeing competing offers. The BCG framing — that acquirers must define specific competitive use cases an acquisition unlocks — is the same logic that makes D&B's Paydex, Buydex, and corporate family trees structurally attractive as embedded infrastructure rather than point solutions.

data_science.tagline: The shared memory layer that turns raw data pipelines into reusable, consistent ML fuel.
data_science.what_it_is: A Feature Store is a centralised data system purpose-built for machine learning. It sits between your raw data sources and your models, handling the creation, storage, versioning, and serving of 'features' — the engineered inputs that models actually learn from. Think of it as a curated, governed library of signals: instead of every data scientist re-computing 'days since last payment' or 'number of active subsidiaries in a corporate family tree' from scratch, the feature store computes it once, names it canonically, and serves it consistently to both training pipelines and live inference endpoints. Feature stores solve two painful ML production problems simultaneously: training-serving skew (your model trained on one version of a feature but gets served a different one at runtime) and feature duplication (ten teams independently building the same Paydex-derived risk signal with subtly different logic).
data_science.how_it_works: A feature store has four core components. (1) Feature Engineering Layer: transformations are defined in code — SQL, PySpark, or Python — and registered with metadata (owner, data lineage, refresh cadence, acceptable staleness). (2) Offline Store: a columnar store (typically Parquet on S3, BigQuery, or Snowflake) optimised for batch retrieval — used to generate training datasets with point-in-time correct joins, preventing data leakage by ensuring a feature value reflects only what was known at the prediction timestamp. (3) Online Store: a low-latency key-value store (Redis, DynamoDB, Cassandra) that serves pre-materialised feature vectors to models in real time — sub-10ms lookups at inference time. (4) Feature Registry: a catalogue with schema, statistics, ownership, and lineage metadata — the governance and discoverability layer. The critical mechanism is the point-in-time join: when building a training dataset, the store joins entity keys (e.g., DUNS Number) and a label timestamp to the feature table, retrieving only the feature value that existed at that exact moment — never the future. This eliminates leakage. Popular open-source implementations include Feast; enterprise options include Tecton, Hopsworks, and Databricks Feature Store (now part of Unity Catalog).
data_science.when_to_use: Use a feature store when: (1) Multiple models share overlapping inputs — avoiding redundant compute and logic drift. (2) You need real-time model serving and batch training to consume identical features — the online/offline consistency guarantee is the store's core value. (3) Regulatory or audit requirements demand feature lineage — knowing exactly which version of a feature powered a credit or risk decision. (4) Your team is beyond the first model and managing feature sprawl across notebooks. (5) You operate with entity-centric data — anything keyed on a business, customer, or asset identifier maps naturally to a feature store's entity-key architecture. Do NOT over-engineer into a feature store for a single model, a pure batch use case with no real-time serving, or a team of one — the operational overhead won't pay off.
data_science.worked_example: D&B's Prospecting Agent serves real-time ICP fit scores to SDRs inside Salesforce Agentforce. The agent scores incoming net-new companies the moment they are entity-resolved to a DUNS Number. Without a feature store, the scoring pipeline re-computes signals like 'trailing-12-month Paydex trend', 'corporate family tree depth', 'Buydex category spend velocity', and 'firmographic peer cluster assignment' at query time — expensive, slow, and inconsistent with how the model was trained. With a feature store: (1) Offline: a nightly Spark job computes all signals for 600M+ entities, does a point-in-time join against labelled won/lost deals, and writes training datasets to the offline store. The model trains on exactly the feature values that existed when each deal closed — no leakage. (2) Online: materialised feature vectors keyed by DUNS Number land in Redis. When the Prospecting Agent resolves a new company to DUNS #123456789, it fires a single Redis lookup, retrieves a 40-dimension feature vector in <8ms, and passes it to the XGBoost scoring model. (3) Governance: the Feature Registry flags 'paydex_12m_trend' as owned by the Risk Data team, refreshed daily, with a 36-hour acceptable staleness threshold — so if the upstream pipeline is delayed, the serving layer alerts rather than silently serving stale scores. The result: training-serving skew is eliminated, every agent archetype (Prospecting, Pipeline Risk, Account Expansion) shares the same canonical signals, and a compliance audit can reconstruct exactly which feature version scored any entity on any given day.
